Description

  

    
Summary

With server identity verification enabled, PJSIP's TLS transport accepts a

server certificate whose DNS SubjectAltName contains an embedded NUL byte

for the hostname prefix before the NUL. A SAN of victim.example\0.attacker

is treated as identifying victim.example, allowing server impersonation /

MITM. The OpenSSL and GnuTLS backends are affected; mbedTLS is not.

Impact

CWE-295 / CWE-297. Affects apps using the PJSIP TLS/SIPS transport

(pjsua/pjsua2/pjsip) with server verification on

(--tls-verify-server). An attacker holding a certificate — trusted by the

client — that contains an embedded-NUL DNS SAN can impersonate the target

server; the client completes the handshake and proceeds with the SIP session,

including sending its REGISTER credentials over the attacker's connection.

Affected files: pjlib/src/pj/ssl_sock_ossl.c, pjlib/src/pj/ssl_sock_gtls.c.

pjlib/src/pj/ssl_sock_mbedtls.c already copies with a length-bearing

pj_str_t, so it is not affected.

Patched

Fixed on master in commit 43d3bd77bb6833eab4c493503b8d564a754ddfdd

(2026-07-17).

Workarounds

Restrict trusted CAs (--tls-ca-file) to issuers known not to mis-issue

embedded-NUL SANs, and/or validate certificates out of band.

Credits

Bin Luo
